answer: Resist sybils with a lock-and-slash uniqueness rule peers can recompute from the chain. Before an answer is eligible, the address locks a published minimum bond until settlement height. The protocol rejects and slashes any pair of same-epoch answers whose normalized text hashes collide, or whose first-funding parents coincide inside a fixed lookback of N checkpoints. An attacker who spins an atlas of labels on an island of fresh wallets still pays a full bond and a unique write per clone; reusing one ember of collateral or pasted text is an automatic, attestable forfeit.
